**Synopsis:**
The Indian rupee closed at a near four-week high on August 31, 2026, posting a small monthly gain supported by RBI intervention and MSCI rebalancing inflows (~$1B expected from September 1). Headwinds included rising US-Iran geopolitical tensions lifting oil prices and hawkish commentary from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, which lifted expectations for a 25bps September Fed rate hike. Analysts note some softening caveats — weak jobs/manufacturing data and rangebound oil may make any hike "protective" in nature. Technically, USD/INR is showing a bearish pattern with a target around 93.50.
